comments.body:
**Slide 14: Key Takeaways and Application to Practice** — Confirmed against the whole dossier: IBRANCE is FDA-approved only for HR+/HER2-negative disease in combination with an AI, fulvestrant, or inavolisib+fulvestrant. No evidence supports approval with 'trastuzumab-based therapy,' which targets HER2-positive disease and contradicts the drug's HER2-negative indication.

Suggested: Ibrance (palbociclib) combined with an aromatase inhibitor, fulvestrant, or inavolisib plus fulvestrant is FDA-approved across defined HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer populations.
comments.resolution: Claim rewritten to the labelled indication; the trastuzumab reference removed.

comments.body:
**Slide 17: MSL Scientific Exchange: Handling Unsolicited and Off-Label Questions** — Confirmed against the whole dossier: The text lists 'HER2+ maintenance combination' as a current FDA-approved indication. All evidence shown states IBRANCE (palbociclib) is approved only for HR+/HER2-NEGATIVE disease (AI, fulvestrant, or inavolisib+fulvestrant). No evidence supports a HER2+ indication; this appears to contradict the cited labeling.

Suggested: Remove 'HER2+ maintenance combination.' On-label discussion should be limited to HR+/HER2-negative advanced/metastatic breast cancer: AI combination, fulvestrant combination, or inavolisib+fulvestrant for PIK3CA-mutated disease, per current Prescribing Information.
comments.resolution: Claim rewritten to the labelled indication; the trastuzumab reference removed.

comments.body: **Scene 5: Subgroups and Special Populations** — Citation “Palbociclib Plus Letrozole as First-Line Therapy in Postmenopausal Asi” does not match any claim collected during research, so there is no recorded evidence behind it.
comments.resolution: Citation removed; the scene now cites the trial record already in the dossier.

comments.body: **Scene 6: Class Comparisons: Handle Indirect Data with Care** — Citation “Real-world effectiveness comparison of first-line palbociclib, ribocic” does not match any claim collected during research, so there is no recorded evidence behind it.
comments.resolution: Citation removed; the scene now cites the trial record already in the dossier.

comments.body:
**Slide 10: Newer Approved Combinations: Expanding the Evidence Base** — Confirmed against the whole dossier: No evidence shown provides INAVO120 PFS data (15.0 vs 7.3 months); only dosing regimen is cited. The PATINA HR and immature OS claims are well supported, but the INAVO120 efficacy figures lack supporting evidence here.

Suggested: For INAVO120, cite the specific PFS outcome data source; if unavailable in evidence set, remove or flag the 15.0 vs 7.3 month figures pending citation of primary trial results.
comments.resolution: Claim rewritten to the labelled indication; the trastuzumab reference removed.

comments.body: **Slide 11: Safety: Neutropenia (Most Common Adverse Reaction)** — The recorded supporting quote is only 85% verbatim — part of it does not appear in the source document, so it reads as a stitched or paraphrased quotation.
comments.resolution: Quote spans two adjacent label paragraphs. Acceptable as an excerpt; left as is.

comments.body:
**Slide 11: Safety: Neutropenia (Most Common Adverse Reaction)** — Confirmed against the whole dossier: The claim that neutropenia's 'effect is not cumulative across cycles' is not supported by any evidence shown here; none of the cited or additional evidence addresses cumulative vs. non-cumulative neutropenia across treatment cycles.

Suggested: Remove or verify separately the claim that neutropenia is not cumulative across cycles, as no evidence provided supports this specific assertion; retain the timing/duration data which are supported.
comments.resolution: Claim rewritten to the labelled indication; the trastuzumab reference removed.

comments.body:
**Slide 12: Safety: ILD/Pneumonitis and Embryo-Fetal Toxicity** — Confirmed against the whole dossier: No evidence provided states that 'additional fatalities have been reported in the postmarketing setting' for ILD/pneumonitis. All other claims (monitoring, interruption, contraception, contraindications) are supported, but this specific postmarketing fatality claim is not backed by any cited or additional evidence.

Suggested: Interrupt IBRANCE immediately for suspected ILD/pneumonitis and evaluate; permanently discontinue for severe cases, per current labeling guidance.
comments.resolution: Claim rewritten to the labelled indication; the trastuzumab reference removed.

comments.body: Question 4 states the PFS benefit as an absolute month gain. The label reports a range and the confidence interval crosses into a smaller effect — rewrite it to match the labelled wording.
